title: P1.11a4 Prove distinct goal briefs through real MCP and durable readback
description: Final P1.11a hardening slice. Extend the strict durable goal catalog for versioned brief-bearing GoalCreated facts while preserving truthful legacy handling, then prove the landed contract, daemon writer, and client edge through the production MCP host rather than a recording port or fixture backend.
definitionOfDone: Verify-or-block first: re-measure the landed contract, authenticated daemon goal.create writer, typed client helper, real MCP host wiring, GoalCreated store writer, and strict goal-catalog consumer; block rather than recreate any missing prerequisite.

The strict goal catalog decodes both legacy GoalCreated facts and the new exact brief-bearing shape without accepting hybrids; new entries expose exact normalized title and instructions bound to the durable event aggregate, project, goal id, and distinct derived planning run.

A production MCP host test authenticates, submits two distinct briefs through the real goal_create tool using the public client helper, and reads both exact normalized briefs through the production durable catalog with distinct goal ids and planningRunRefs; the generated case count is asserted nonzero.

The same MCP request replays without another durable decision/event and a same-identity changed brief refuses BOOTSTRAP_COMMAND_BYTES_CONFLICT at DAEMON_PREREQUISITE; authority extras refuse INPUT_INVALID at PAYLOAD_SHAPE and all refusal arms prove no mutation.

Contract, daemon, and control-room-client focused tests plus typechecks run standalone with exit 0 and nonzero test-count lines; repo-wide pnpm typecheck and pnpm test are recorded as path-attributed baseline-versus-delivered evidence.

An adversarial review confirms no demo/fixture backend, fixed live run, caller authority field, permissive legacy/hybrid decoder, or second command authority remains; production mutations for brief persistence and refusal each make the named integration assertion red before restoration.
taskRails: P1.11a1, P1.11a2, and P1.11a3 must land first; relaxing any premise would let an integration-shaped test certify a substitute.
Use the real MCP host and the production SqliteEventStore/catalog reader; recording dispatch ports and hand-seeded GoalCreated rows are not acceptance evidence.
Legacy rows may remain explicitly brief-unknown, but missing prose must never be invented or upgraded to authority.

TWO PLAN CORRECTIONS, both forced by measurement, both making the proof MORE production-shaped:
1. IN-PROCESS SEEDING IS IMPOSSIBLE. The plan said to seed with `driveThrough(store, "project.activate")` and close the handle before spawning. Measured: the host then refuses to start — `moe-mcp-stdio exited 1 before answering: GENESIS_RECOVERY_BINDING_FAILED: GENESIS_INSTALL_REFUSED (RECOVERY_INITIAL_INSTALL_HISTORY_PRESENT)`. A daemon will not adopt a store that already carries history. The whole six-command bootstrap chain (project.register, project.bind_repository, provider.probe, policy.install, policy.validate, project.activate) is therefore driven THROUGH the host too, each with its identity taken from the affordance surface and only its body supplied by the fixture constants. Strictly better evidence: nothing in the durable store was written in-process.
2. `policy.validate` MUST NOT NAME AN ACTOR. The fixture's `evaluationInput` sets `actor: "principal-1"`, which is fine in-process but refuses over MCP with `BOOTSTRAP_POLICY_ACTOR_UNBOUND` at DAEMON_INGRESS: bootstrap-policy-services.ts:130 requires `input.actor === request.principalId`, and a real session's principal is not the fixture's. The suite drops `actor` and lets the daemon bind it — which is the property the seam exists to enforce.

NORMALIZATION IS OBSERVABLE AND CONTENT-ASSERTED. Both briefs carry surrounding whitespace, a CRLF, NFD marks and a 4-byte code point (U+1F680 / U+1F9EA). The read-back must EQUAL the normalized form and must NOT equal the submitted raw bytes (both directions asserted), and the astral code point is asserted to survive — so a reader echoing the caller, or folding characters, fails.

CHECKOUT-DURABILITY MEASUREMENT, added beyond the step text. The spawned host runs WORKTREE bytes, and apps/daemon/src/http/affordance-read.ts carries uncommitted foreign WIP that makes goal.create repeatable with a freshly minted target; at HEAD the offer is pinned to the single `goal-live-1` subject. Rather than assume the proof survives that difference, the suite submits a THIRD brief whose envelope reuses the FIRST submission's targetAggregateId — the exact shape a fixed-subject offer produces — and it is accepted (`EFFECTS_COMMITTED`) with its own `goal-${commandId}` and its own brief. So the proof binds to the AUTHENTICATED COMMAND IDENTITY, not to the uncommitted affordance behaviour, and does not become false at a clean checkout. The offer's targetAggregateId is never asserted anywhere.

Store counts are snapshotted after seeding and after the two submissions: decisions delta is exactly 2. Teardown closes the driver and calls `removeWorkspace`, which throws on a leaked child — the orphan detector is live.
